Findings: 0 CRITICAL, 0 HIGH, 0 MEDIUM, 0 LOW across correctness, security (code-level), maintainability and test-adequacy. CR-009-1 (MEDIUM, round 1) is RESOLVED. is_owner_message() now rejects records with isCompactSummary true (a structural flag) and the exact stripped text '[Request interrupted by user for tool use]' in both string and list-text forms. The exclusion is exact-match, so an ordinary message quoting the marker still counts as the owner. The refusal signal (toolDenialKind) is still not string-matched. Regression tests cover: a user-rejected refusal lists past the marker; an automode-blocked refusal lists past a compaction summary; a typed reply after either still clears; an Esc interruption with no refusal creates no item; a message quoting the marker is still the owner. Corpus re-measure on the candidate: compaction summaries classed as owner 8 -> 0; tool-use interruption markers 2 -> 0 (the other 16 r1 'markers' are the plain Esc text '[Request interrupted by user]', which still counts as the owner by design, since the owner pressed Esc); every one of the 15 denials is now first followed by a typed record carrying permissionMode (user-rejected 2/2, automode-blocked 12/12, permission-rule 1/1), so no measured refusal is cleared by a synthetic record. No regression: a compaction summary or marker is still a user-role lastTurn, as before, so D2 prose behaviour is unchanged; PARSER_VERSION stays 8. The comments state why the exclusions exist, with no process narration.
